findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all existing custom grant factories
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory adds `String getShortcut()` with no default implementation. Any third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory outside this repo will fail to compile/link after upgrade. It should have a default (e.g. return UNKNOWN/"na") to remain backward compatible.

findings.title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) silently removed
findings.body: The diff deletes the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from the public SPI class OAuth2GrantType.Context. External grant implementations or decorators that copied context will break at compile/runtime. Removal is unrelated to adding grantType and should be retained or deprecated.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher logic inverted and offset wrong
findings.body: In `isAccessTokenId` the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when the shortcut matches and true when it differs, so tests pass for wrong grants and fail for correct ones. The offset is also wrong: a 6-char prefix encodes session(0-1), token(2-3), grant(4-5), so grant must be `substring(4,6)`, not `substring(3,5)`.

findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice, never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType,...)` twice, the second time with message about rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and later causes NPE in `encodeTokenId()` when concatenating `':' + rawTokenId` or in decoding logic.

findings.title: Decoding attacker-controlled token id throws unchecked exception
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId() throws IllegalArgumentException for wrong prefix length or unknown shortcuts. The encoded id comes from the `jti` of a presented access token, i.e. attacker-controlled. Any future caller using it on introspection/userinfo/token-exchange paths will turn a malformed/forged token into a 500 instead of invalid-token handling. It should return UNKNOWN context or throw a handled OAuth error.

findings.title: No enforcement that grant shortcuts are 2 chars breaks fixed 6-char format
findings.body: Encoder/decoder assume `session(2)+token(2)+grant(2)=6` chars and throw if length !=6. Nothing validates `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` length (javadoc even says 3-letters). A custom grant returning 1, 3, or longer shortcut will produce IDs that can never be decoded, causing IllegalArgumentException/IllegalStateException at token creation or validation.
